text.approach: From the Lightning Creek trailhead on Ross Lake, the first-ascent party hiked east past Willow Lake, then left the trail to bushwhack through timber and avalanche debris, crossed a ravine, and climbed steep dirt and brush to open timber on the broad shoulder south of the peak. They reached meadows near 5,000 ft and bypassed cliff bands to a saddle at about 6,200 ft below the buttress — roughly six hours from the trailhead — where they bivouacked.

text.approach: A two-stage approach and the second stage is the part that stops people. Day one is a long haul of 11-plus miles under heavy loads from the road to a camp just north of the peak - the same Hozomeen Ridge / border-swath ground used by the north-side scrambling routes, reached from Silver-Skagit Road out of Hope, B.C. From that camp the approach to the base took the first ascent party a tedious and painstaking 4.5 hours: downclimb a loose third-class gully, which the party described as dangerous but the lesser of the two evils, then cross several precipitous rocky ribs and steep, unstable ground to traverse into the launch point below the wall. Budget the base approach as a half-day objective in its own right and do it in daylight. Confirm the NPS border-gate status before planning; the crossing at Hozomeen has been closed to vehicles and foot traffic since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026.
